item.title: 'Tech Titan' Arora spearheads $1bn shot at NBA's London basketball team
item.description: The US technology billionaire who led the acquisition of English cricket's most lucrative Hundred franchise is in talks to buy London's new NBA Europe team.
item.media:description: San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama shoots over Oklahoma City Thunder guard Ajay Mitchell (25) and Isaiah Hartenstein, center, during Game 2 of the Western Conference finals of the NBA basketball playoffs Wednesday, May 20, 2026, in Oklahoma City. (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)

item.title: BP hangs for sale sign over North Sea operations
item.description: BP has placed its North Sea oil and gas business up for sale.
item.media:description: The UK government is being sued after it granted BP a new drilling licence in the North Sea

item.title: Betfred to cut 600 jobs as 132 shops close amid industry tax raid
item.description: One of Britain's biggest high street bookmakers is to axe hundreds of jobs as it prepares to close more than 130 shops amid a deepening tax raid on the industry.
item.media:description: Betfred bookmakers sign on their shop in Chinatown in London. (Photo by Dave Rushen / SOPA Images/Sipa USA)

item.title: Sainsbury's agrees £120m deal to sell Argos
item.description: Sainsbury's has revealed it is selling Argos under a "business as usual" deal that will allow the company to concentrate on its core grocery business.
item.media:description: A customer shops at the Argos store inside a Sainsbury's supermarket in Richmond, West London, Britain February 21, 2024. REUTERS/Isabel Infantes

item.title: Apple warns of memory chip shortage for key devices
item.description: Apple has warned it is seeking alternative memory chip suppliers as "very significant" constraints threaten future sales of its key devices.

item.title: Key HS2 contracts renegotiated as government scrambles to slash costs
item.description: Two of the High Speed 2 (HS2) railway's most significant private sector deals have been renegotiated, the government will announce on Friday, as it tries to demonstrate that Britain's biggest infrastructure white elephant is finally under control.
item.media:description: HS2 staff walk through the Chilterns tunnel at West Hyde, Hertfordshire, as the HS2 project continues. Pic: PA

item.title: Former Newcastle backer Staveley eyes Gold stake in West Ham United
item.description: The financier who backed the takeover of Newcastle United Football Club alongside Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund is in talks to buy a minority stake in West Ham United, the newly relegated Championship club.
item.media:description: The London Stadium, home of West Ham United football club. File pic: Reuters

item.title: Indonesian FA president vows to back World Cup sell-off despite growing backlash
item.description: The president of the Indonesian football association has vowed to vote in support of FIFA president Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell a multibillion dollar stake in the World Cup's commercial rights, even as global opposition to the proposals gathers momentum.
item.media:description: FIFA's President Gianni Infantino apologises to English fans for "joke" he made about their arrest record at previous World Cup

item.title: Poundland owner joins suitors for department store chain Harvey Nichols
item.description: The owner of Poundland has tabled an offer for Harvey Nichols as the owner of the Knightsbridge-based department store chain nears a decision about its future.
item.media:description: Harvey Nichols department store in Knightsbridge, London. PRESS ASSOCIATION Photo. Wednesday August 14, 2013. Nick Ansell/PA Wire.
